detail: The train-51 TCP_NOTSENT_LOWAT-only repair was refuted on hbox: the stopped-reader test observed 581632 queued octets against a 147456 limit. TCP_NOTSENT_LOWAT supplies writable notifications; eager nonblocking writes can still fill available send-buffer space. The old send-window theorem modeled a false write-refusal premise and has been replaced. host/native/mux.lisp now observes Linux SIOCOUTQNSD before each plan render, calls ACL2 fn-send-window-render-p, and parks the exact unrendered continuation when refused. POLLOUT retries admission; the send-progress timer remains live while no output buffer exists. books/send-window.lisp states NOTSENT + PENDING < W + Q for legal traces with one writer, exact observations and a maximum wire quantum Q; a no-transmit trace renders less than W + Q in total. defteeth covers the host quantum bound, the composed trace bound, and the stalled-reader bound, including removal of admission. fn-send-window-render-p-by-definition connects the deployed decision to fn-sw-render-p. TLS/compression expansion must be included in Q; the arithmetic does not certify those facilities, ioctl correctness, preflight scans or in-flight unacknowledged bytes.

notes.author: Codex / lane send-window-2
notes.note: Statement-first replacement of the false kernel premise. The host observation fails closed on ioctl failure or unsupported platforms. The /proc/net/tcp native test includes in-flight data and retains its existing receive-window slack. Gates and native results are recorded in the lane bundle handoff.

title: F5: four stopped one-octet readers of 512 KiB articles degrade the fast clients' p99 6.2x and grow the owner 87.6 MB: the kernel send queue is an unbounded render-ahead
